fields.meta_title: Time Sheet Form That Totals Hours | Emergent
fields.meta_description: What a time sheet form should collect, how to set one up, and an app that deducts unpaid lunches and splits out overtime before approval.
fields.h1: Build a Time Sheet Form That Does the Math
fields.hero_description: Build a time sheet form that turns clock times into weekly hours, with lunch breaks taken out and overtime split for approval.
fields.features_heading: Hours Counted the Way Payroll Reads Them
fields.features_subheading: A printable sheet leaves the adding to whoever checks it on Friday. Emergent's version does the math as each day goes in.
fields.feature_1:
Daily totals from punch times

Turns each day's punch-in and punch-out times into hours, minus breaks, then adds the days into a week. Nobody types a total, and no supervisor re-adds a column to check it.
fields.feature_2:
Unpaid meal breaks deducted

Subtracts meal breaks of 30 minutes or more and keeps short rest breaks in the day's hours. The Department of Labor treats short breaks as paid time and meal periods as unpaid.
fields.feature_3:
Overtime kept in its own column

Moves any time beyond 40 hours in the workweek into a separate overtime column. The supervisor approves both figures together, and your payroll provider applies the rate.
fields.feature_4:
A job or client code on each entry

Asks for a job number or client code on every line and returns any entry left blank. Hours then roll up per code, ready for a job costing report or the next client invoice.
fields.feature_5:
Approval that locks the sheet

Sends each submitted sheet to the employee's supervisor in Slack or email. Approved entries lock, and any later edit needs a reason and records who changed it and when.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take anywhere

Exports the full codebase to your GitHub repo on paid plans. Extend it later with a payroll API sync or a kiosk clock-in screen, or ask Emergent for either one in a new prompt.

fields.usecase_heading: Time Sheet Forms by Type of Work
fields.tab_content_1:
Which of the 43.5 hours count as overtime

Overtime starts after hour 40. A warehouse associate works five days with a 30-minute unpaid lunch each day. The form deducts every lunch, totals the week at 43.5 hours and separates the 3.5 past 40. Federal law requires overtime pay for those unless she is exempt, and her supervisor approves them first.
fields.tab_content_2:
Every hour lands on a job number

Construction payroll and job costing read the same sheet. A site foreman logs a crew of five against Job 2207 and Job 2214, and the form totals each job as entries arrive. One six-hour entry came in with no job code. It goes back to the worker to fix and stays out of both totals until then.
fields.tab_content_3:
Proof of each visit, signed by the client

Home care runs on visits, not shifts. An aide taps start when she arrives at a client's home and finish when she leaves. Before she goes, the client signs on her phone screen. The visit reaches the agency's scheduler with the signature attached, and its 2.5 hours land on the aide's time sheet.
fields.tab_content_4:
Who still owes a sheet by Monday

Payroll can only run on sheets that exist. The pay period closes Sunday night. On Monday morning a Slack message tells the office manager that 10 of 12 sheets are approved and two never came in. One click sends both people a reminder, and each late sheet goes to its supervisor once it is submitted.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Time Sheet Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to a time sheet form that settles break and overtime rules up front and leaves the arithmetic to the form.
fields.howto_step_1_des: Choose the period payroll already runs on, weekly or biweekly. It sets how many rows the sheet needs and when it closes. Overtime is counted per workweek, and a biweekly sheet needs a subtotal for each of its two weeks.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Have people enter when they started and finished each day, plus the length of any break, instead of a typed total. Totals entered by hand drift by quarter hours. Times let the form do the math and show when each shift happened.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Federal rules count short rest breaks as hours worked and treat a real meal period as unpaid. Give each its own field, start the deduction at 30 minutes, and show it on the sheet so the employee can check the math.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Keep regular hours and anything over 40 in a workweek in separate columns. Nonexempt employees earn at least time and a half for those extra hours under federal law. Check your state's rules too, then show both totals to the approver.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Add job codes where hours get billed
fields.howto_step_5_des: When hours feed job costing or a client invoice, add a job or client code to each entry. Make it a dropdown of open jobs instead of free text. Entries with a blank code go back before the week closes.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Route every sheet to one approver
fields.howto_step_6_des: Send each sheet to the employee's direct supervisor when the period ends, with a reminder for anyone who has not submitted by the next morning. Lock approved sheets so later edits need a reason and leave a trail.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Keep every approved sheet and every edit in one place for at least two years, the period the Department of Labor gives for time cards. At each close, export approved hours to payroll split into regular and overtime.

plan.angle: The live SERP is printable templates (Pinterest, Template.net, Notion, a fillable PDF, Jotform's construction form) and an AI Overview listing the fields a time sheet needs. None of them adds the hours up for you or knows who still owes a sheet. This page answers what a time sheet form should collect and how to set one up, then builds what a template cannot: entries that total themselves with unpaid lunches deducted, hours past 40 flagged, hours tied to job numbers, client sign-off on a phone, and reminders before the pay period closes.

faq_plan.q: What is a time sheet form?
faq_plan.a: A time sheet form is the record of the hours one person worked in a pay period. Each day shows when work started and stopped and any unpaid break, with a total for the day and the week. A supervisor approves it, and payroll pays from the approved hours.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a time sheet form?
faq_plan.a: Decide the pay period and the approver, then list what each day needs: start time, finish time, break length, and a job code if you bill hours. Describe that in plain English to Emergent's AI form builder. Emergent builds the form, its totals, and the approval step from that prompt, and you change any of it by prompting again.

faq_plan.q: What fields should a timesheet form include?
faq_plan.a: Give it the employee's name, the pay period dates and one row per day with a start time, finish time, and break length. Then add a daily total, a weekly total, and a line for the approver's name and the date approved. Leave out any column the approver will not read.

faq_plan.q: How do paid days off show up on a time sheet form?
faq_plan.a: Give leave its own row type, such as vacation, sick, or holiday, with the hours paid for it. Keep those hours in their own total, apart from hours worked. The approver then sees both numbers on one sheet. Days already approved through a time off request form can fill those rows before the employee opens the sheet.

faq_plan.q: How should a time sheet form handle a shift that runs past midnight?
faq_plan.a: Record the date with each start and finish time, not the clock time alone. A shift from 10:00 PM to 6:30 AM then totals 8.5 hours instead of a negative number. Count the hours on the date the shift started, and use that rule for every overnight shift.

faq_plan.q: Who should approve a time sheet form?
faq_plan.a: Have the employee's direct supervisor approve it, since that person knows which shifts were worked. Name one backup approver for vacations. No sheet then sits unapproved through the payroll close. In an app built with Emergent, Slack, email, and in-app alerts handle the reminders and escalations.

faq_plan.q: Can hours from a time sheet form help with performance reviews?
faq_plan.a: Yes, as attendance facts such as late submissions and missed punches. Treat them as one input next to the manager's notes, because hours say nothing about the quality of the work. With Emergent, that data lives in a database you own, and an employee evaluation form can draw on the same records.

faq_plan.q: Should a time sheet form be daily or weekly?
faq_plan.a: Pick daily for crews that move between job sites, and weekly for staff on a fixed schedule. A daily sheet is submitted at the end of each shift, while the details are fresh. A weekly sheet gives the approver one review per person per week, and a biweekly period holds two of them.

faq_plan.q: Do time sheet forms have to follow a set format?
faq_plan.a: No. The Department of Labor says the Fair Labor Standards Act requires no particular form for the records. It does require data about the hours worked and the wages earned. Any layout you choose has to capture each day's hours. Check your state's rules as well.

faq_plan.q: How do I log training hours on a time sheet form?
faq_plan.a: Give training its own entry type with start and finish times, and tag it with the course name. Payroll then sees those hours apart from regular shifts, and you can report hours per course. A training feedback form can collect what attendees thought of the session, kept separate from the hours.

truth.evidence: All five DOL facts match their quotes (overtime past 40 at time and a half; short breaks compensable; meal periods not compensable; two-year retention for time cards; no particular form required). Numbers add up: 8.5x4+9.5=43.5, 3.5 past 40; jobs 130 and 64; 9:00 to 11:30 = 2.5; 10+2=12. Claims map to approved ids (alerts, code-export, e-signature-capture, database-owned, api-connect). Legal points stay informational with 'Check your state's rules' and 'your payroll provider applies the rate'.
